zh.principle: **协议**：证书吊销列表（Certificate Revocation List）。RFC 5280 摘要写明它「profiles the X.509 v3 certificate and X.509 v2 certificate revocation list (CRL) for use in the Internet.」§3.3 描述机制：「This method involves each CA periodically issuing a signed data structure called a certificate revocation list (CRL).」并定义其内容——「A CRL is a time-stamped list identifying revoked certificates that is signed by a CA or CRL issuer and made freely available in a public repository.」定位方式很窄：「Each revoked certificate is identified in a CRL by its certificate serial number.」§5.1.2 列出必填字段：「The required fields identify the CRL issuer, the algorithm used to sign the CRL, and the date and time the CRL was issued.」
zh.why: 选择 CRL 的理由是分发成本：§3.3 说「CRLs may be distributed by exactly the same means as certificates themselves, namely, via untrusted servers and untrusted communications.」依赖方则要同时看签名与状态——「that system not only checks the certificate signature and validity but also acquires a suitably recent CRL and checks that the certificate serial number is not on that CRL.」为让缓存与新旧比较可判定，§5.2 强制两个扩展：「Conforming CRL issuers are REQUIRED to include the authority key identifier (Section 5.2.1) and the CRL number (Section 5.2.3) extensions in all CRLs issued.」§5.2.3 解释作用：「The CRL number is a non-critical CRL extension that conveys a monotonically increasing sequence number for a given CRL scope and CRL issuer.」
zh.used: 撤销触发条件被列举，§3.3 含「Such circumstances include change of name, change of association between subject and CA」以及「compromise or suspected compromise of the corresponding private key.」时间字段有硬约束：§5.1.2.5 说「Conforming CRL issuers MUST include the nextUpdate field in all CRLs.」§5.1.2.4 规定编码分界——「CRL issuers conforming to this profile MUST encode thisUpdate as UTCTime for dates through the year 2049.」空列表也有规则：§5.1.2.6「When there are no revoked certificates, the revoked certificates list MUST be absent.」§5.3 建议携带原因：「CRL issuers SHOULD include reason codes (Section 5.3.1) and invalidity dates (Section 5.3.2) whenever this information is available.」
zh.broken: 历史条目不能提前消失：§3.3 规定「An entry MUST NOT be removed from the CRL until it appears on one regularly scheduled CRL issued beyond the revoked certificate's validity period.」§6.3 的校验算法假定有取新机制：「if the next update time of a CRL has passed, the algorithm assumes a mechanism to fetch a current CRL and place it in the local CRL cache.」可处理性也有限制，§5.2 说「If a CRL contains a critical extension that the application cannot process, then the application MUST NOT use that CRL to determine the status of certificates.」并且 CRL 不是唯一手段：§3 写「Revocation status information may be provided using the Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) [RFC2560], certificate revocation lists (CRLs), or some other mechanism.」§5 允许 CA 不出 CRL：「Conforming CAs are not required to issue CRLs if other revocation or certificate status mechanisms are provided.」
zh.history: RFC 5280 署名 D.Cooper、S.Santesson、S.Farrell、S.Boeyen、R.Housley 与 W.Polk，2008 年 5 月发布，头部标「Obsoletes: 3280, 4325, 4630」。§1 把它定位成标准族的一部分：「This specification is one part of a family of standards for the X.509 Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) for the Internet.」§5.1.1 记录 CA 的密钥选择：「MAY use one private key to digitally sign certificates and CRLs, or MAY use separate private keys」。§8 澄清保密性不是前提：「Since certificates and CRLs are digitally signed, no additional integrity service is necessary.」

en.principle: **Protocol**: Certificate Revocation List (证书吊销列表). The abstract of RFC 5280 says it "profiles the X.509 v3 certificate and X.509 v2 certificate revocation list (CRL) for use in the Internet." §3.3 describes the mechanism: "This method involves each CA periodically issuing a signed data structure called a certificate revocation list (CRL)." and its content — "A CRL is a time-stamped list identifying revoked certificates that is signed by a CA or CRL issuer and made freely available in a public repository." Identification is narrow: "Each revoked certificate is identified in a CRL by its certificate serial number." §5.1.2 lists the mandatory fields: "The required fields identify the CRL issuer, the algorithm used to sign the CRL, and the date and time the CRL was issued."
en.why: Distribution cost is the reason CRLs exist: §3.3 notes "CRLs may be distributed by exactly the same means as certificates themselves, namely, via untrusted servers and untrusted communications." Relying parties check both signature and status — "that system not only checks the certificate signature and validity but also acquires a suitably recent CRL and checks that the certificate serial number is not on that CRL." To make caching and supersession decidable, §5.2 mandates two extensions: "Conforming CRL issuers are REQUIRED to include the authority key identifier (Section 5.2.1) and the CRL number (Section 5.2.3) extensions in all CRLs issued." §5.2.3 explains the purpose: "The CRL number is a non-critical CRL extension that conveys a monotonically increasing sequence number for a given CRL scope and CRL issuer."
en.used: Triggers are enumerated, §3.3 including "Such circumstances include change of name, change of association between subject and CA" and "compromise or suspected compromise of the corresponding private key." The time fields carry hard rules: §5.1.2.5 states "Conforming CRL issuers MUST include the nextUpdate field in all CRLs." and §5.1.2.4 sets the encoding boundary — "CRL issuers conforming to this profile MUST encode thisUpdate as UTCTime for dates through the year 2049." Empty lists are specified too: §5.1.2.6 "When there are no revoked certificates, the revoked certificates list MUST be absent." §5.3 recommends detail: "CRL issuers SHOULD include reason codes (Section 5.3.1) and invalidity dates (Section 5.3.2) whenever this information is available."
en.broken: History cannot be dropped early: §3.3 requires "An entry MUST NOT be removed from the CRL until it appears on one regularly scheduled CRL issued beyond the revoked certificate's validity period." §6.3 assumes a refresh path: "if the next update time of a CRL has passed, the algorithm assumes a mechanism to fetch a current CRL and place it in the local CRL cache." Processability has limits, §5.2 saying "If a CRL contains a critical extension that the application cannot process, then the application MUST NOT use that CRL to determine the status of certificates." And CRLs are not the only route: §3 records "Revocation status information may be provided using the Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) [RFC2560], certificate revocation lists (CRLs), or some other mechanism." while §5 permits a CA to skip them: "Conforming CAs are not required to issue CRLs if other revocation or certificate status mechanisms are provided."
en.history: RFC 5280 is signed by D. Cooper, S. Santesson, S. Farrell, S. Boeyen, R. Housley and W. Polk, published May 2008 with "Obsoletes: 3280, 4325, 4630" in the header. §1 places it in a standards family: "This specification is one part of a family of standards for the X.509 Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) for the Internet." §5.1.1 records the key choice available to a CA: "MAY use one private key to digitally sign certificates and CRLs, or MAY use separate private keys". §8 clarifies that confidentiality is not assumed: "Since certificates and CRLs are digitally signed, no additional integrity service is necessary."

zh: TBSCertList：待签名的 CRL 主体。
thisUpdate：本次 CRL 的签发时刻。
CRL number：单调递增的序列号扩展。
reason code：条目级的撤销原因。
delta CRL：仅携带增量的列表。
en: TBSCertList: the to-be-signed body of a CRL.
thisUpdate: when this CRL was issued.
nextUpdate: the deadline for the next CRL.
CRL number: the monotonically increasing sequence extension.
reason code: the per-entry revocation reason.
Delta CRL: a list carrying only changes.
